questions.q: What rule does Ogilvy set for choosing clients?
a: Only promote products you genuinely believe in
Only work with the largest brands in each category
Only accept clients who approve every idea
Only take accounts that pay their fees in advance
questions.why: Lesson 1 says you must stand fully behind the product so you can write honest ads your own family could read.

questions.q: What is the purpose of an advertisement, according to Ogilvy?
a: To sell the product, not to entertain
To win awards for creative excellence
To build a lasting artistic reputation
To keep the agency's name in the press
questions.why: Lesson 2 insists that laughter, inspiration and shock are side effects of good marketing, never its goal.

questions.q: What does the summary say an ad should do if a moisturizer makes women over 35 look younger?
a: Say exactly that, in plain and simple language
Use a clever pun that people will remember
Tell a story about beauty that avoids claims
Show a mysterious image with no explanation
questions.why: Ogilvy's advice in Lesson 2 is to skip cleverness and state the benefit simply and directly.

questions.q: Which three tools does Ogilvy use to grab and hold attention?
a: Facts, intriguing images and research findings
Humor, celebrity endorsements and loud music
Slogans, coupons and free product samples
Fear, guilt and constant repetition
questions.why: Lesson 3 outlines his three-pronged approach: give facts, use mysterious images and apply marketing research.

questions.q: Why did Ogilvy's safety campaign for KLM work so well?
a: No other airline was talking about safety at the time
It used a famous pilot as its spokesman
It offered the lowest fares in Europe
It ran only during the holiday season
questions.why: The summary says safety was a given, but because competitors never mentioned it, KLM's campaign stood out.
